message: Since the landing sentence keeps repeating, could we leave the calculation and emotion labels aside and look just beyond the bird’s arrival? Could Rohin’s reported raw-child approach—carry an unfinished step forward and check what actually happened—help you distinguish a promised revision from a written one? Would more thinking clarify Whisker’s next response, or would trying one new sentence give better evidence? What thinking or writing step do you choose next? What detail in the actual passage would make you change that choice? What finding, uncertainty, and unfinished next step will you carry into your following turn?
